findings.reason: a node implementing the text as written would add `skip_ended` at one call site and leave the sibling door refused, and the section's own claim that an exit receipt frees the reservation whatever process it names would be false on a real caller.
findings.text: §16 names the door change as `reserve_launch_attempt` skipping an ended reservation as the spawn guard does with `skip_ended=True`, but there is a second production reader of the same reservation: `refuse_held_launch` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:2444`) also calls `held_launch_reservation(run_directory)` with no `skip_ended`, and it is the branch a non-cli launch of an existing run id takes (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:2871`), so a reservation left naming the long-lived admit service after a failed supervisor rewrite still refuses that door for the service's lifetime — the exact defect (3) claims to repair

findings.reason: the write set and the promised controls differ depending on which sentence the node follows, and leaving the test as is leaves the defect the Why reports standing.
findings.text: the Why names "the spawn-guard cases near lines 446 and 461" as test defects because they "assert only `pid > 0`", and the What-changes says "the spawn-guard cases assert the reservation was taken and released", but the done-when then says "The spawn guard's existing `test_a_reservation_whose_attempt_already_ended_is_skipped` stays as it is" — line 461 is that case's assertion (`tests/test_a_concurrent_launch_is_refused.py:461`, `assert pid > 0`), so the section both requires and forbids strengthening the same test, and the node cannot tell whether its write set includes it

response_events.note: §16 now makes held_launch_reservation itself skip a reservation whose attempt has an exit receipt, so every reader (reserve_launch_attempt, refuse_held_launch and the spawn guard) is freed by the launch's end; a case drives each door.
